raw.assessment: The incumbent plausibly handles stable courses adequately: unchanged-assignment centers had seven-minute median handling, versus 17 overall. Its sampled course-set accuracy was 80%, below the 95% target. Assignment changes accompany six affected exports, supporting investigation of current-assignment selection without establishing causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation: apparent absence could involve naming or comparison. Replacement delivery greatly exceeds execution time, but elapsed waiting is not measured active handling. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course center.

openings.claim: Selecting courses using current instructor assignments may misrepresent requested-week membership; stable course identifiers plus week-effective membership could reduce these errors.
openings.delta: Test historical inclusion semantics behind the existing CSV export while independently testing whether renames merely disguise present courses.
openings.prediction: With names held fixed, changing only the current assignment changes incumbent inclusion for an identical requested week; week-effective selection removes that dependence. A rename-only discrepancy may persist in coordinator recognition despite correct membership.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, replay fixed-week cases varying assignment and name separately, plus a split-course case across center boundaries. Compare exported course membership with explicit fixture expectations, check CSV compatibility and continue attendance writes. Estimate history availability, engineer effort and hosting cost before choosing a bounded implementation.
assumptions: Week-effective membership can be established reliably.
A correction can fit six engineer-days and existing hosting without blocking attendance entry.

openings.claim: Does reconciling course identity consume most active handling, or does substantial work remain when the course set is already verified?
openings.delta: Separates export-selection improvements from downstream spreadsheet work that current logs cannot reveal.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, prior course-set verification sharply reduces checking time; if importing dominates, verified files retain substantial handling time.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions for counterbalanced fabricated tasks with matched documented-schema files, one with an independently verified course mapping. Time checking, correction, downloading and importing separately; record replacement waiting separately from active work. Keep sessions inside authorized workspaces and cap engineering support within six days.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary spreadsheet work.
Independent verification reflects each coordinator's intended course set.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports; they do not establish causation. Replacement delays exceed execution time. One opening links possible export-induced checking demand to a different course-selection interface; timetable reliability and implementation cost remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: Organizing historical exports through current assignments may generate apparent omissions, triggering checking and replacement requests; replacement jobs using the same selection rule may reproduce that demand. A center-owned, week-specific course manifest could remove the need to reconstruct intended membership from today's instructor assignment.
openings.delta: Counterfactual: forbid current instructor assignment as the selector for past weeks. Instead, a coordinator confirms a reusable center/week manifest in the private service; the exporter selects its course identities and emits the documented CSV. Renames retain identity; splits require explicit membership decisions. The removed dependency formerly supplied course association, access filtering, and labels if those functions share the assignment join. Replacement dependencies: authorized center ownership and independent row authorization; stable course identities or a bounded identity mapping; explicit week boundaries and intended membership; an accountable manifest updater and timely schedule information; week-appropriate label/split mapping; declared attendance cutoff with consistent nonblocking reads; the existing CSV serializer. Whether assignment joins actually carry these obligations must be inspected before removal.
openings.prediction: With attendance and intended membership held constant, changing only today's instructor assignment or course name should leave manifest-selected membership unchanged. If selection causes the observed demand, coordinators should request fewer replacements and spend less total time, including manifest upkeep; unchanged demand would weaken the hypothesis.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging fixtures covering reassignment, rename, split, and foreign-center rows. Across two sessions each, six coordinators use both interfaces in counterbalanced order; record checking, manifest maintenance, corrections, download/import time, and replacement requests. Test concurrent attendance entry and CSV compatibility. Proceed only if the bounded implementation fits six engineer-days and existing hosting; then assess the next 40 exports against all stipulated targets.
assumptions: Current assignment or name-based selection contributes to omissions.
Coordinators can establish intended weekly membership reliably.
Manifest upkeep costs less than the checking it removes.
Independent authorization, identity mapping, and consistent reads can fit the resource cap.

critiques.assumption: Historical membership or coordinator confirmation can establish the intended weekly course set reliably.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 establishes heterogeneous schedule sources, while timetable completeness and update timing are explicitly unmeasured. Neither proposal supplies historical membership availability. This supports a missing-evidence critique, not a finding that manifests are wrong.
critiques.opening: Test whether explicit discrepancies between historical candidates and local schedules improve membership decisions before treating either source as authoritative.
critiques.comparison: Z1 depends on reliable history; A1 depends on reliable confirmation and affordable upkeep. Their hybrid may expose disagreements but cannot discover omissions shared by both sources.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: fabricate stale-history, stale-timetable, and shared-omission cases with separately authored expected membership; assess detection and correction. No operational tests have been performed.

critiques.assumption: Providing independently verified membership predicts the net handling benefit of obtaining that verification routinely.
critiques.limitation: Z2 can isolate checking costs but does not itself establish affordable verification. A1 already counts upkeep; that accounting must survive the hybrid.
critiques.opening: Charge all preparation, confirmation, correction, and import work to the comparison.
critiques.comparison: Faster downstream checking can coexist with unchanged or increased total handling.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: record verification production time as well as coordinator use time.

openings.claim: A week-effective candidate manifest with visible uncertainty and coordinator correction may reduce total reconciliation work.
openings.delta: Combine Z1's historical candidates with A1's explicit weekly decisions; use Z2's activity timing. Smallest assessable capability: a private staging candidate list, discrepancy display, and stable-identity overrides. Reliable dated membership remains a missing dependency.
openings.prediction: Compared with Z1 alone, correction catches visible history errors; compared with A1 alone, prepopulation reduces upkeep. The interaction fails when both sources omit the same course or discrepancy review costs exceed saved work.
openings.probe: Proposed: compare incumbent, Z1, A1, and hybrid on matched fabricated tasks across twelve coordinator sessions, counterbalancing order and counting all work. Include rename, split, foreign-center, CSV, and concurrent-entry checks; estimate effort before implementation.
openings.fit: uncertain; preserves private processing, documented CSV, concurrent attendance, six engineer-days, and hosting allowance. Subsequent 40 exports must retain median handling at most 12 minutes, at least 38 correct course sets, and zero foreign-center records.
assumptions: Staging results transfer; they cannot establish operational target attainment.
